newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares hit new high after U.S. payrolls data.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares hit new high after U.S. payrolls data.

text.p: Dutch shares reversed moderate early losses to close mainly firmer on Friday after a surprise fall in U.S. September non-farm payrolls.
Payrolls - a closely watched measure of job growth and economic strength - fell 40,000 versus expectations of a rise of 166,000, triggering sharp gains for bond and stock prices.
Amsterdam rose with other markets, the AEX of 25 Dutch blue chip shares closed up 3.34 points at a new all-time closing high of 584.93 with 19 of the constituent shares showing gains.
"After the U.S. data client buying and professional short covering pushed up prices over a broad front," a dealer said.
Before the payrolls figures came out, share prices had drifted off on profit-taking amid apprehension that unfavourable figures could erode some of the market's recent gains.
But dealers said the market looked well underpinned now and that with the Dow poised to break through the 6,000 mark, Dutch shares should also see new highs next week.
